data.name: Tibaldo
data.gender_notes: Tibaldo is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Latin 'Theodaldus' or 'Theobaldus', derived from 'Theos' (God) and 'Baldeus' (gift) or 'bald' (bold) – a god-given, bold name. The name Tibaldo carries the meaning “God's gift” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Tibaldo usually hope their child will grow to embody god's gift and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Tibaldo belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's gift.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Tibaldo total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_greek.name: Τιμπαλδο
in_greek.long_meaning: Τιμπαλδο είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από τη γερμανική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'εκλεκτός του Θεού'. Το όνομα αυτό προκύπτει από τις γερμανικές λέξεις 'tieb' που σημαίνει 'αγαπητός' και 'wald' που σημαίνει 'εξουσία' ή 'δύναμη'. Το Τιμπαλδο χρησιμοποιείται ως προσωνύμιο για εκείνον που έχει τύχει της εύνοιας του Θεού και είναι εκλεκτός.

in_latin.name: Tibaldo
in_latin.long_meaning: Tibaldo is a name derived from Germanic roots, signifying 'God's beloved'. It combines 'tieb', meaning 'beloved' or 'dear', with 'wald', meaning 'rule' or 'power'. In Christian tradition, Tibaldo represents one who is cherished and favored by God, embodying divine love and grace.

in_english.name: Tibaldo
in_english.meaning: Tibaldo means a person beloved by God
in_english.long_meaning: Tibaldo is a Christian name with Germanic origins, meaning 'beloved by God'. It is derived from the Germanic words 'tieb', meaning 'beloved' or 'dear one', and 'wald', meaning 'power' or 'ruler'. The name Tibaldo has been used in Christian tradition to signify a person who is highly favored and loved by God. Historically, the name Tibaldo has been associated with strength, courage, and devotion. It symbolizes a deep connection with the divine and reflects the values of faith, hope, and love.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Tibaldo" carries a rich cultural history within the Christian tradition. As a derivative of 'Theodaldus' and 'Theobaldus', it is a reminder of the secure faith that the early Christians had in God's protection and provision. This name has a robust connection to kingship, especially in medieval Europe, where Theobald of Blois, the Count of Champagne, was a renowned political and military leader and advocate for peace and justice.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Tibaldo, meaning "brave and strong in God," embodies the courage and strength that comes from deep faith and trust in the divine. This name inspires its bearer to face life's challenges with unwavering determination and unyielding spirit.

historical_references.context: Tibaldo was the son of Count Odalric II of Spoleto and a grandson of the Lombard prince, Grimoald III of Benevento. He became the Duke of Spoleto in 1032, and in 1045, he was given the title of Marquis of Ancona by Emperor Henry III. Tibaldo expanded his territory and, in 1047, he gained control of the Duchy of Spoleto after defeating Arduin of Mantua. In 1052, he was involved in a power struggle with Pope Leo IX, which ultimately resulted in his excommunication. He died in 1057.

historical_references.context: Tibaldo was a member of the powerful Naples Angevins, who ruled over the Kingdom of Naples. He was the son of Charles of Anjou, the Count of Naples, and Beatrice of Provençe. In 1270, Tibaldo was granted the city and territory of Sorrento by his father. He became a powerful lord in the region, and in 1294, he was appointed as the Admiral of the Kingdom of Naples by his brother, King Charles II. Tibaldo played an important role in the defense of the kingdom against the French invasion led by Robert II of Artois. He died in 1316.
